tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

1	//! Стратегия — одна функция `on_event<MD, B: Bot<MD>>` (A6, D-СТРАТЕГИЯ,
2	//! таск 15). Идёт в `Backtest` крейта (`lob/backtest.rs:506`, шаг 6.3) и, в
3	//! фазе 2, в `LiveBot` — без единой правки: обе стороны реализуют один и тот
4	//! же `hftbacktest::types::Bot<MD>`, и это то самое A6 «стратегия пишется под
5	//! `Bot<MD>` крейта».
6	//!
7	//! Экономические примитивы не переизобретены здесь второй раз — это была бы
8	//! Reinvention (`interfaces.md`, правило 5): вход мейкером у своей стороны
9	//! спреда, время жизни входа, горизонт выхода и знак стороны уже названы и
10	//! проверены в `lob::backtest` (`entry_side`, `entry_price`, `exit_price`,
11	//! `ENTRY_TTL_NS`, `HOLD_NS`, `SIGMA_LONG`/`SIGMA_SHORT` — все `pub`), и этот
12	//! файл их переиспользует как есть. Разница с `backtest::drive_cell` — не в
13	//! экономике сделки, а в форме: `drive_cell` управляет временем бэктеста
14	//! пакетно, по заранее известному списку сигналов (`&[Signal]`), и не может
15	//! быть вызвана на живом сокете, где будущих событий не существует.
16	//! `on_event` — ровно одно событие за вызов, без `elapse`/`wait_*` внутри
17	//! себя: кто и когда продвигает часы стороны — решает вызывающий (тест ниже
18	//! и, в фазе 2, реальный live-цикл), а не эта функция.
19	//!
20	//! `best_prices` ниже — единственная реализация в `src/` (находка ревью,
21	//! таск 17): `lob::backtest` больше не держит одноимённый приватный хелпер
22	//! (снесён при переработке движка на очередь), так что копировать здесь
23	//! нечего — оставлена своя, потому что вызывающему (`on_event`) нужна ровно
24	//! эта проверка `INVALID_MIN`/`INVALID_MAX` перед тем же `entry_price`/
25	//! `exit_price` из `lob::backtest`.
26	
27	use hftbacktest::depth::{MarketDepth, INVALID_MAX, INVALID_MIN};
28	use hftbacktest::types::{
29	    Bot, Event, OrdType, Side as HbtSide, Status, TimeInForce, EXCH_BUY_TRADE_EVENT,
30	    EXCH_SELL_TRADE_EVENT,
31	};
32	
33	use crate::lob::backtest::{
34	    entry_price, entry_side, executed_notional, executed_qty, exit_price, ENTRY_TTL_NS, HOLD_NS,
35	};
36	
37	/// Лучшие цены стороны как `(bid, ask)`, `None` — книга неполна
38	/// (`best_bid_tick`/`best_ask_tick` ещё на `INVALID_MIN`/`INVALID_MAX`,
39	/// до первого снапшота).
40	fn best_prices<MD: MarketDepth>(depth: &MD) -> Option<(f64, f64)> {
41	    if depth.best_bid_tick() == INVALID_MIN || depth.best_ask_tick() == INVALID_MAX {
42	        return None;
43	    }
44	    let (bid, ask) = (depth.best_bid(), depth.best_ask());
45	    if bid.is_finite() && ask.is_finite() && bid > 0.0 && ask > 0.0 {
46	        Some((bid, ask))
47	    } else {
48	        None
49	    }
50	}
51	
52	/// Снимок ног входа по ордерам крейта (F4, В-78): накопленное исполненное
53	/// (`qty − leaves_qty`; у крейта `exec_qty` — объём **последнего** исполнения,
54	/// а не сумма), стоимость исполненного (`executed_notional` — по всем
55	/// исполнениям ноги, R7) и признак
56	/// «вход ещё решается» — в рынке стоит хоть одна нога или её запрос
57	/// (постановка/снятие) ещё не подтверждён биржей.
58	///
59	/// `Bot::position` крейта для этого не годится: `Local` обновляет позицию
60	/// только на `status == Filled`, поэтому частично исполненная нога (модель
61	/// очереди по объёму, F3) остаётся `PartiallyFilled` и позиции не даёт —
62	/// находка F3. Считается по ордерам (`orders(asset).get(&id)`), без кучи и без
63	/// `HashMap`: ног у плана единицы, лишних структур на пути события нет.
64	struct EntrySnapshot {
65	    /// Накопленное исполненное по всем ногам входа.
66	    qty: f64,
67	    /// Накопленная стоимость исполненного по всем исполнениям ног (R7).
68	    notional: f64,
69	    /// Вход ещё решается: нога стоит в рынке или её запрос летит.
70	    open: bool,
71	}
72	
73	/// Снять снимок ног входа `first_id .. first_id + legs`. Нога, которой в учёте
74	/// крейта уже нет (биржа её не знает — терминальна и снята с учёта), вход не
75	/// держит: считать её «решается» значило бы ждать её вечно.
76	fn entry_snapshot<MD, B>(bot: &B, asset_no: usize, first_id: u64, legs: u8) -> EntrySnapshot
77	where
78	    MD: MarketDepth,
79	    B: Bot<MD>,
80	{
81	    let mut snap = EntrySnapshot {
82	        qty: 0.0,
83	        notional: 0.0,
84	        open: false,
85	    };
86	    for i in 0..u64::from(legs.max(1)) {
87	        let Some(order) = bot.orders(asset_no).get(&first_id.saturating_add(i)) else {
88	            continue;
89	        };
90	        if order.req != Status::None
91	            || matches!(order.status, Status::New | Status::PartiallyFilled)
92	        {
93	            snap.open = true;
94	        }
95	        let executed = executed_qty(order);
96	        if executed > 0.0 {
97	            snap.qty += executed;
98	            snap.notional += executed_notional(order);
99	        }
100	    }
101	    snap
102	}
103	
104	/// Сдвиг уровней стопа и тейка к **средней цене исполненного** входа (F4,
105	/// В-78). Форма задаёт стоп и тейк расстояниями от цены входа, поэтому, когда
106	/// реальная средняя другая (частичное исполнение, лестница), оба уровня
107	/// сдвигаются на ту же разницу — расстояния формы сохраняются.
108	///
109	/// Средняя приводится к сетке тиков (цены живут на тиках, так же поступает
110	/// крейт при постановке), поэтому сдвиг — целое число тиков; при полном
111	/// исполнении по плановой цене он **ровно ноль** (обе величины — произведение
112	/// одного и того же целого числа тиков на шаг), и числа прежних прогонов не
113	/// меняются — на этом стоит гейт «те же круги» (F3/F4).
114	fn level_shift(entry_vwap: Option<f64>, entry_px: f64, tick_px: f64) -> f64 {
115	    let Some(vwap) = entry_vwap else {
116	        return 0.0;
117	    };
118	    if !vwap.is_finite() || !entry_px.is_finite() || tick_px <= 0.0 {
119	        return 0.0;
120	    }
121	    let snapped = (vwap / tick_px).round() * tick_px;
122	    if (snapped - entry_px).abs() < tick_px * 0.5 {
123	        0.0
124	    } else {
125	        snapped - entry_px
126	    }
127	}
128	
129	/// Стоит ли лучшая цена стороны **на уровне касания** (B4, В-58 п. 5):
130	/// «касание не кончилось» — цена не ушла ни в отскок, ни сквозь уровень.
131	/// Сравнение с точностью половины тика: цены собираются умножением целых тиков
132	/// на шаг, и равенство `f64` здесь было бы проверкой арифметики, а не рынка.
133	/// Уровень берётся со стороны входа: у лонга (бид-уровень) это лучший бид, у
134	/// шорта — лучший аск. Выключенный или неполный план (`tick_px = 0`) не даёт
135	/// «прилипания»: считать его на неизвестном шаге — выдумывать признак.
136	fn still_at_level(entry_side: HbtSide, bid: f64, ask: f64, level_px: f64, tick_px: f64) -> bool {
137	    if tick_px <= 0.0 || level_px <= 0.0 {
138	        return false;
139	    }
140	    let side_px = match entry_side {
141	        HbtSide::Buy => bid,
142	        _ => ask,
143	    };
144	    (side_px - level_px).abs() < tick_px * 0.5
145	}
146	
147	/// Потолок ожидания подтверждения отмены — предохранитель фаз `CancelPending`
148	/// (вход) и `ExitCancelPending` (лимитка выхода), один механизм на обе (F8b,
149	/// В5/Р2 аудита 21.09).
150	///
151	/// Число — решение владельца 2026-09-21 (В-79): 1 с. Измеренная В-68 задержка
152	/// снятия по WS trade с боевого сервера: медиана 3.98 мс, p95 4.55, p99 5.01,
153	/// max 5.42 мс (100 циклов); REST-хвост до 15.5 мс. Потолок в ~200 раз выше
154	/// измеренного p95 и в ~70 раз выше REST-максимума, поэтому **при задержке
155	/// снятия В-68** в бэктесте он не срабатывает (числа прежних прогонов не
156	/// меняются — гейт «те же круги» это проверяет: `f3-queue-gate.sh` требует
157	/// нулей `n_entry_cancelled_cancel_timeout`/`n_exit_cancel_timeout`). Это
158	/// свойство измеренных RTT, не общее: сетка с `--median-rtt-ns cancel=` выше
159	/// потолка включит его, и колонки это покажут. В живом контуре потолок
160	/// освобождает круг, если подтверждение отмены не пришло: без него фаза ждёт
161	/// биржу бесконечно, сигналы суток теряются (ровно то, ради чего закрывался Б1).
162	///
163	/// Срабатывание — не «отмена прошла»: заявка могла остаться в рынке, поэтому
164	/// потолок только освобождает круг под управлением плана (`Holding` при
165	/// позиции), а причина называется `CancelTimeout` — видно в `forms.csv`.
166	/// Сама заявка становится **сиротой** (F8c, К1): снятие повторяется на каждом
167	/// событии в любой фазе, исполнение сироты считается и гасится
168	/// (`StrategyState::sweep_orphans`).
169	pub const CANCEL_WAIT_NS: i64 = 1_000_000_000;
170	
171	/// Фаза одного круга. Спрятана от вызывающего (`interfaces.md`: модуль
172	/// `lob/strategy` «прячет: триггер, состояние») — снаружи виден только
173	/// `Action`, возвращённый из `on_event`.

175	enum Phase {
176	    /// Ждём случая войти: следующий валидный тик со спредом — и есть
177	    /// триггер (D-ОРДЕР: цена и размер к этому моменту уже известны заранее,
178	    /// сборка кадра на живом пути — забота `commands::lob::react`, не эта

Entry filters are not in `src/lob/strategy.rs`. Every existing entry gate is a pre-signal filter on the touch record (`TouchRecord`), checked in `TouchFilter::admits` in `sets.rs`. The strategy only places the entry after it gets a signal, and it cannot see anything before the touch. `src/lob/cells.rs` has nothing to do with filters: it is the cluster bootstrap for statistics.

## 1. How an entry filter flows (template: `usd_min`, wall notional)
- **CLI:** filters are keys of `--set <name>:k=v,…` (`args.rs:280-281`). Only `age`, `flow`, `side` and `frontrun` also exist as command flags (`args.rs:213-229`). `usd_min` exists only as a set key.
- **Set struct:** `FilterSet` holds `usd_min: Option<f64>` (`sets.rs:52`). It defaults to `None` in `from_args` (`sets.rs:234`) and in `parse` (`sets.rs:263`). The key is parsed at `sets.rs:293-302`, and the error text listing known keys is at `sets.rs:343`.
- **Filter struct:** `TouchFilter.usd_min` (`sets.rs:383`), filled by `from_day` (`sets.rs:401`) and `from_set` (`sets.rs:427`).
- **Day params:** `DayParams.usd_min` (`drive.rs:361`), set in `bounce_grid.rs:563`.
- **Check:** `TouchFilter::admits` at `sets.rs:472-476` rejects the touch when price × size (in dollars) is below `m`.
- **Call site:** `drive.rs:70-78`. A rejected touch counts as `skipped` and never becomes a `BounceSignal`, so `on_event` never runs for it. The same filter is also used by `fill_capacity.rs:669-673`.
- **Header:** `plan.rs:435-457`.
- **Where a new filter goes:** a field in `FilterSet`, `TouchFilter` and `DayParams`, a key in `parse`, and a check in `admits`. The value it tests must be a field on `TouchRecord` (`levels.rs:525-609`). That field is computed by `LevelTracker` (`levels.rs:1272`) in its per-level `Live`/`Touch` state (`levels.rs:786`, `levels.rs:866`). It also needs a column in the touches cache, as T2 did for `depth_behind_lots`.
- If the filter needs a new cache column, copy the fail-fast check at `bounce_grid.rs:303-310`, which refuses to run on an old cache that lacks the column.

## 2. What `on_event` sees
- The backtest creates one `StrategyState` per signal at `t0` (the touch start), so the strategy only sees events after the touch.
- **Book:** through `bot.depth(asset_no)`, the hftbacktest `MarketDepth` trait, implemented by `Book` (`book/mod.rs:324`). There is no per-level add/cancel delta stream.
- **Trades:** through `bot.last_trades(asset_no)`, a buffer with capacity 64 (`backtest.rs:646`). The driver passes it to `state.observe_wall_trades(...)` and then clears it (`backtest.rs:1579-1580`, `1607-1608`). The eaten-by-trades logic is at `strategy.rs:1032-1074`.
- **Wall in strategy state:** it is part of the plan, `TradePlan::Bounce` (`strategy.rs:312-417`): `level_px`, `level_qty` (size at signal), `level_floor_qty`, `tick_px`. The side comes from `StrategyState.sigma` (`strategy.rs:523`). The running fields are `level_qty_at_entry`, `level_qty_max` and `eaten_qty` (`strategy.rs:542-549`). There is no first-seen time in the strategy; wall age is `TouchRecord::age_ms()` (`levels.rs:613`) = `start_ms − level_birth_ms`.
- **Pre-touch history lives in `levels.rs`**, which already sees trades and book frames:
  - ring `flow_ring: [i64; FLOW_WINDOW_MIN]` (`levels.rs:1303`)
  - strength-sample ring `sh_ts`/`sh_e2: [i64; STRENGTH_HIST_SLOTS]` (`levels.rs:908`)
  - `traded_first_s` (`levels.rs:579`)
  - `births: VecDeque` (`levels.rs:1275`)
- **Fixed-size arrays in the strategy:** `EntryLadder` `[_; MAX_ENTRY_LEGS=8]` (`strategy.rs:232-243`) and `OrphanCarry` `[_; MAX_ORPHAN_BATCHES=4]` (`strategy.rs:613-621`). There are no ring buffers there.

## 3. BTC price
- The strategy has no BTC price. The backtest runs one asset per symbol.
- The BTC gate is a context axis on the set: `ctx` over `CTX_AXES` (`sets.rs:59-66`), with keys `btc1h`/`btc2h`/`btc3h`/`btc4h` + `_min`/`_max`.
- Values come from `--regime-from` per-minute CSVs written by `regime.py` (`read_regime_day`, `sets.rs:105-156`), matched to the touch minute in `touch_contexts` (`sets.rs:161-181`) and checked in `admits` at `sets.rs:479-489`.
- The B-104 main variant uses `btc4h_max=-44.55` with `age=2700,side=bid` (`docs/findings/p02-block-b-2026-09-26.md:49`).

## 4. Output bytes
- **Columns:** `ROUNDS_HEADER[16]` (`outputs.rs:30`), `FORMS_HEADER[35]` (`outputs.rs:55`, the last 2 only with carry), `SIGNALS_HEADER[11]` (`outputs.rs:120`). A filter adds no column.
- **Header line:** the `# lob bounce-grid: …` line (`plan.rs:435`) is written into every CSV (`outputs.rs:262-278`). It prints `usd_min={:?}` and `eaten_min={:?}` always, so adding a new always-printed field would change the bytes.
- To keep bytes identical when the filter is off, copy the T-35 pattern (`plan.rs:446-450`): print the key only when it is `Some`. With the field left as `None`, `admits` is unchanged and so are the rows.

## 5. Definitions from the docs
**Г-36 (iceberg)** has three versions:
- *Level version* (`P-02-batch-wall-entry.md:823-826`): "`size_monotonic=false` И `traded_lots / max(size_max,1) ≥ 1,0`". The 1.0 threshold sits between p99.9 and p99.99 on 3 August days.
- *Causal per-touch version* (`:289-296`): flag for touch k if the "сумма `traded_during` касаний с `touch_index < k` ≥ `size_max_before` касания k". It is compared only among `touch_index ≥ 1`.
- *On approach A* (`:426-428`): past touches with `end_ms < A`, sum of `traded_during` ≥ max(`size_at_arm`, `size_max_before` of those touches).
- Result (`:448-452`): flag 1 occurred 0 times in August and in September, so it is "не определена как фильтр". The "fast restore within a few frames" idea (H6, `:63`) was never made operational without the trade tape.

**Г-07 (depth behind the wall):** `depth_behind_lots` = "сумма размеров той же стороны книги строго дальше от середины, чем уровень, на кадре начала касания" (`levels.rs:599-608`; `P-02…:473`). The filter keeps the top tercile, with bounds frozen on August (`:436-437`, `:761-780`, commit `172b51d`). Main version on `.50` (rough), neighbour on `.200`.

**Г-55** (`hypothesis-pool-2026-09-25.md:178`): only a sentence — the cause of the wall being eaten (outside BTC factor vs the owner selling) decides whether the move continues. Data: "сделки + свечи (BTC)". It was never tested, and there is no formula or window.

**Г-140** (`hypothesis-pool…:190`): queue-reactive — tell a market-wide shock from a local event by the queue intensities (add / cancel / trade), not by hourly BTC windows. Source: Huang–Lehalle–Rosenbaum 2015. Data: `.50` event intensities from the binlog. Never tested, and there is no formula or window.

## 6. Depth `.200`
- The live collector subscribes to `orderbook.50` and `orderbook.200` (`bybit/conn.rs:42,61`; `ws.rs:14-23`). `.200` is written to `root/deep/` (`COMMANDS.md:413,419,428`: ~2.8 GB/day). It is never read by anything and is auto-deleted after the nightly pull (`:425`).
- The docs say `.200` exists only for 15–21.09 or 15–24.09 (`P-02…:95`, `:562`; `hypothesis-pool…:414-416`), and that "Августа для Г-07 нет вообще".
- **This conflicts with the code and another doc:** `lob import-archive` converts Bybit `…_ob200.data.zip`, i.e. the `orderbook.200` stream at 100 ms, into the main binlog (`import_archive.rs:4-16`). The August epoch `e-aug` is that archive, "ob200 + сделки" (`docs/findings/august-oos-2026-09-24.md:15`), and 01–15.09 (`e-archive`) is imported the same way. `Book` holds up to 256 levels per side (`book/mod.rs:99-110`).
- So August and early-September replays probably already contain 200 levels, and only the own-recorded days from 16.09 on have `.50` in the main file. I have not checked whether `depth_behind_lots` on August really used more than 50 levels; that needs confirming before trusting the docs' "August = rough `.50`" label.
